notes: The session's web-search allowance was already spent when this part began (all six searches tried were refused), and the fetch tool could not look up campaign addresses, so every page was opened directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), one request at a time, robots.txt obeyed: the campaign websites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State (learned from a scratch copy of the database on which the kit's own files step had been run; the real database was only read), each county's, city's and school district's own site, the Minnesota DFL's endorsed list, the Legislative Reference Library, and Wikipedia.

Not reached, and nothing worked around: emilythabesformn.com and the inner pages of erikskogquist.com (HTTP 429 on every try, so Emily Thabes has no website finding here although she filed that address); milesfor742.com and the St. Louis County Schools site (no answer); the Republican units for House 21A, 39A and 58B (no address found without a search; mncd7gop.com did not answer), so no Republican endorsement is recorded for Krist Wollum, Andy Macko or Drew Roach; the Minnesota Judicial Branch site, which earlier parts found answers 403, was not asked, so Judge Robert Docherty has no findings.

Read and left out on purpose: Anders Folk's birth date on Wikipedia (it carries no citation) and Wikipedia's dates for his time as Acting U.S. Attorney; Drew Roach's birth date on Wikipedia (the article gives two different days; he is a sitting legislator with a record page); Scott Grice's post as Pine County chief deputy (a job, not an office); party posts, association and church boards, labor and personal endorsements; family, schools and employers on every page read. Drew Roach's own-words quote speaks of his 2024 endorsing convention, not 2026.

Candidates not on their government's current list of members, and so with no official page: Rodney Altena (Pipestone County lists another District 2 commissioner), Bob Redig (Winona County), Steven Haes (Lakeville), Ryan Reider (Champlin), Mark Gransee (Kasson-Mantorville), Vincent Miles (St. Cloud), Felicia Reed (Litchfield) and Melissa Roberts (White Bear Lake). Norman County's and Cloquet's board pages showed no member names to a plain reader.
